researchQuestion: Can a bounded retrieval-assessment-rewrite loop improve evidence coverage over the frozen single-pass RAG baseline without unacceptable false positives, latency, or cost?

baseline.retrieval: single dense query with metadata filtering

safetyAndReproducibility: The existing production baseline is unchanged.
Every retrieval query, compact ranked result, assessment, rewrite, duration, attempt, and stop reason is recorded.
Repeated normalized query plans terminate the loop.
Invalid empty or oversized rewrite plans fail validation.
The controller is dependency-injected so planner variants can be compared without changing orchestration.
Ranking-merge policies are injectable and the deterministic highest-score merge is only the default foundation behavior.
No prior non-selected comparative rewrite is enabled by default.

plannedBenchmark.singleChangedVariable: single-pass retrieval versus bounded agentic retrieval
primaryMetrics: both-side evidence coverage for comparative cases
plannedBenchmark.selectionPolicy: Must be preregistered before any validation execution. Production remains disabled until a variant passes every retrieval and safety guardrail.

latestOutcome.reason: Raw audit showed MAX_TOKENS on both the initial 256-token response and its single controlled recovery after 10 of 70 validation cases.

knownLimitations: The foundation does not select an assessor or rewrite model.
Score and language coverage gates measure evidence availability, not semantic entailment.
Agentic generation and final answer quality are outside this foundation commit.
